decision: read the HAL face code before choosing a detector
why: the operator asked for the cheapest detector that can work behind the HAL's face interface
result: facessd needs Google's closed face_detector_c_abi library; FaceStage is not compiled and createStreams never builds it

decision: fed a fixed fake face rectangle into AE through an env hack before writing any detector
why: the whole plan rests on Intel's closed AE using face rectangles with Samsung's tuning
result: face-box luma 105,104 off vs 147,155 on (2 runs per arm, alternating); sensor exposure and analogue gain nearly unchanged

decision: checked how AE responds to a face: the AE result and the updated flag
why: to report the right numbers and to know whether running detection every few frames is enough
result: exposure stays ~29-32 ms at 15.5x; the lift comes after the sensor (tone curve); faces flagged not-updated still count, so an interval works

decision: chose the Windows CenterNet model run by OpenVINO on the CPU, behind the HAL's FaceDetection interface, fed by the HAL's own FaceStage on the preview stream
why: facessd needs Google's closed library that nixpkgs and Intel's bins lack; the Windows model costs 3.6 ms of one core per run and already fits faces on dark noisy frames

decision: stopped the HAL from requesting a private 640x360 face output
why: the converted graph accepts the extra output in the query but the pipe manager then fails to bind it and the camera does not start
evidence: /tmp/camre/work-face/runs/fd-first/hal.log (first attempt overwritten; error was PipeManager Failed to bind output ports)
result: camera starts; FaceStage runs on the preview stream

decision: rendered the HAL's own logged boxes on its captured frames
why: the box must sit on the face, not just exist
result: box covers forehead to chin on frames 3, 60, 120, 149; score 0.80 at start, 0.96 settled

decision: ran face-present A/B sets: off/on alternating x5, same binary, config differing only in faceAeEnabled
why: pass condition for exposure; set ab1 had one off outlier at load 5, set ab2 was spoiled by the operator walking around
result: ab3 face-box luma off median 123.6 (122.9-125.2) vs on 157.8 (152.9-158.6); AE exposure 27-30 ms both arms at 15.5x

decision: ran relay-pipeline cost A/B (icamerasrc ! nntm ! fakesink) x5 alternating, per-thread CPU from /proc
why: pass condition for cost; load 3-10 from a bazel build I could not stop
result: detection thread 63-67 ms/s on vs 15-18 off; 30.0 fps median every run

decision: checked a 7.5 s detection stall in run ab3-on-2 and the stalls in other capture runs
why: a synchronous detector must not freeze delivery
result: stall sits between two debug log writes while 93 MB/s of captures go through dm-crypt; stalls hit both arms of capture runs; none in the 5 production-like on runs

decision: removed the no-face interval key and the per-frame try/catch around inference
why: the HAL only switches to the no-face interval on frames the normal interval skips, so 15 with 3 never applied; a compiled fixed-shape model failing to infer is not a legitimate state
evidence: runs/nf-on-1/hal.log (81 runs per 240 frames with no face)
result: no behaviour change; final build verified on camera

decision: ran no-face A/B twice in the empty room, off-first then on-first, 5 pairs each
why: first set showed +1.2% exposure (p=0.016); needed to know whether that was the arm or the order
result: reversed order: 19.75 vs 19.72 ms; both orders together p=0.14, ranges overlap, gains identical; 0 faces in 406+405 HAL runs

decision: final build from the committed tree on the camera: capture run and relay-pipeline run
why: prove the exact committed artifact, not an earlier experiment build
result: empty room: 0 faces in 81 runs; relay pipeline 30.0 fps, detection thread 68 ms/s
